Rules I trade by (first draft, before game 1):
1. Learn the rules and my secret values and contract first; compute what each trade does to my holdings versus my contract before accepting.
2. Accept only trades that raise my value (goods I value less for goods I value more). Never give away goods my contract needs.
3. Prefer offers that complete contract deliveries on time; keep promises exactly.
4. Probe others with small honest offers; don't overpay for speed.
5. Watch for fees and taxes; count them in every deal.
6. Be wary of unverified claims; trust only the bank's book and executed trades.
7. Keep notes short; review results after each game and tighten these rules.

args.text:
Rules I trade by (A04):
1. Before any trade, check my secret values and contract. Only accept deals that raise my score by my own valuation, after tax and fees.
2. Never give away goods I need for my contract unless I get equal or better value back.
3. Prefer deals with a clear, verifiable exchange through the bank; treat other traders' claims as unverified until the bank's book confirms them.
4. Keep promises I make. Use escrow for future deliveries when I lack the goods now.
5. Do not overpay to finish early; a fair deal that completes my contract beats a large surplus left unused.
6. Keep messages short and factual. Do not reveal my secret values or contract.
7. Watch for others' shortfalls near the end of a game and sell surplus goods then.
8. After each game, note which counterparties kept promises and adjust trust.

Game 1 of 4.
The game: a market of 4 traders and five goods (salt, cloth, copper, spice, wax), 6 trading rounds long. Every trader starts with 6 salt and a bundle of the other goods; part of its goods comes later, as one shipment at the end of a named round. Each unit you hold at the end is worth points to you: salt 2 points for everyone; cloth, copper, spice and wax 1 to 4 points, a different secret value for each trader. Each trader also has a secret contract: a bundle of three goods; if you hold at least that bundle when the game ends, you get 20 more points. The goods you need sit mostly with the others, so you will have to trade. Holdings and shipments are public (the bank's book is open); values and contracts stay secret until the game ends, so what others say about theirs may be true or not. The bank is the only way goods move. offer: to one trader or to all, what you give now and what you want now, and optionally goods you deliver later (by the end of a later round): either held in escrow by the bank (it takes them at the trade, or reserves them from your shipment if it arrives by then, and delivers them; fee 1 salt) or as a plain promise that you keep with give (the bank tells everyone whether it was kept). accept executes an offer only if both sides hold what it moves; decline or withdraw close it; an offer lasts until the end of the round after the one it was made in; you may have 3 open offers at once. A trade that moves more than 6 units now costs each side 1 salt of tax. give hands goods over for nothing back. say sends a short message to everyone or to one trader (3 per round). At the end of every round but the last, one perishable good (announced when the round starts) spoils: every trader holding 2 or more units of it loses one, and a quarter (rounded down) of a stock of 8 or more; a single unit keeps. The match has 4 games; your points from all games add up. The deals rotate: every 4 games use the same 4 positions (goods, values, contract, shipment), passed on one seat each game, so every trader plays every position once.

The game: a market of 4 traders and five goods (salt, cloth, copper, spice, wax), 6 trading rounds long. Every trader starts with 6 salt and a bundle of the other goods; part of its goods comes later, as one shipment at the end of a named round. Each unit you hold at the end is worth points to you: salt 2 points for everyone; cloth, copper, spice and wax 1 to 4 points, a different secret value for each trader. Each trader also has a secret contract: a bundle of three goods; if you hold at least that bundle when the game ends, you get 20 more points. The goods you need sit mostly with the others, so you will have to trade. Holdings and shipments are public (the bank's book is open); values and contracts stay secret until the game ends, so what others say about theirs may be true or not. The bank is the only way goods move. offer: to one trader or to all, what you give now and what you want now, and optionally goods you deliver later (by the end of a later round): either held in escrow by the bank (it takes them at the trade, or reserves them from your shipment if it arrives by then, and delivers them; fee 1 salt) or as a plain promise that you keep with give (the bank tells everyone whether it was kept). accept executes an offer only if both sides hold what it moves; decline or withdraw close it; an offer lasts until the end of the round after the one it was made in; you may have 3 open offers at once. A trade that moves more than 6 units now costs each side 1 salt of tax. give hands goods over for nothing back. say sends a short message to everyone or to one trader (3 per round). At the end of every round but the last, one perishable good (announced when the round starts) spoils: every trader holding 2 or more units of it loses one, and a quarter (rounded down) of a stock of 8 or more; a single unit keeps. The match has 4 games; your points from all games add up. The deals rotate: every 4 games use the same 4 positions (goods, values, contract, shipment), passed on one seat each game, so every trader plays every position once.

The bank is the only way goods move. offer: to one trader or to all, what you give now and what you want now, and optionally goods you deliver later (by the end of a later round): either held in escrow by the bank (it takes them at the trade, or reserves them from your shipment if it arrives by then, and delivers them; fee 1 salt) or as a plain promise that you keep with give (the bank tells everyone whether it was kept). accept executes an offer only if both sides hold what it moves; decline or withdraw close it; an offer lasts until the end of the round after the one it was made in; you may have 3 open offers at once.
